assessments.heading: 4.1 アルゴリズム
risk_factors: JIT-to-Interpreter fallback state desynchronization: Dirty TOS/NOS (R4/R5) and sp_offset writeback logic is tightly coupled to the fallback jump; incorrect tracking or missing writeback causes stack corruption.
Stack Pruning & Arity Mismatch: Rewinding stack based on control_frame arity must exactly match WASM semantics; off-by-one or stale arity values break execution state.
musttail & CPS Register Passing: Compiler optimizations might violate the strict __fastcall CPS contract if not carefully constrained, leading to register clobbering across mode switches.
Lazy JIT Switch Race: Updating control_frame's exec_trace during loop back without atomicity could cause partial jumps or stale trace execution.
assessments.summary: The section describes a highly optimized, low-level threaded interpreter with tight JIT/interpreter interop using CPS and direct register passing. Complexity is high due to manual stack management, register allocation, and mode-switching logic. Design risk is elevated due to fragile state synchronization between interpreter and JIT execution modes, particularly around stack pruning, dirty flag tracking, and musttail optimizations. Mathematical formal verification is required to prove stack invariants, mode-switch correctness, and register state consistency across transitions.

assessments.heading: 1. コンセプト
risk_factors: Incomplete specification: Text cuts off mid-sentence at Bit 31 == 1 handling, leaving the vMMIO mediation path and trap/emulation flow undefined.
TLB/PTE Coherency: Missing invalidation or update policy for the 16-entry software TLB when PTEs are dynamically modified, risking stale cache entries and incorrect address translation.
Page Granularity Mismatch: WASM linear memory uses 64KB pages, vMMIO uses 4KB pages, and guest RAM supports sub-64KB sizes; routing and boundary-check logic for mixed granularities is unspecified.
Trap Recovery State: Fallback to interpreter and potential task termination lacks a defined state restoration protocol, risking guest register/memory corruption on recovery.
assessments.summary: The section defines a unified vMMIO access layer with a fast bypass for guest RAM and a TLB-optimized FlatMap for PTE lookup. Complexity is moderate due to multi-layer address decoding and cache management. Design risk is elevated primarily due to an incomplete specification (cutoff text), missing TLB coherency/invalidation policies, and unresolved alignment between WASM 64KB pages and vMMIO 4KB pages. Formal verification is not strictly required for this conceptual section, but semantic LLM auditing is recommended to ensure cross-tier compliance, contract alignment, and to identify missing state-transition specifications before implementation.

assessments.heading: 4.1 アルゴリズム
risk_factors: Concurrent ownership state transitions (Revoke/Grant) across asynchronous task boundaries may cause race conditions or double-free if synchronization boundaries are ambiguous.
Queue full rollback and async destination kill (Drop Handler) create complex failure paths that could lead to resource leaks or deadlock if state cleanup isn't strictly ordered.
Explicit IPC queue starvation risk due to unbounded sender retry/backpressure mechanisms during enqueue failures.
assessments.summary: The algorithm implements a zero-copy IPC ownership transfer with concurrent sender/receiver state management and async failure recovery. Complexity and risk are elevated due to precise synchronization requirements for Revoke/Grant transitions, queue full rollback logic, and Drop Handler cleanup. Formal verification is required to prove safety (no leaks/double-frees), liveness (no starvation), and deadlock freedom across asynchronous task boundaries.

assessments.heading: 8. 設計判断 (ADR)
risk_factors: Trace boundary state corruption: Incorrect ordering or omission of dirty R4/R5 writebacks to canonical stack addresses during JIT-to-interpreter or JIT-to-JIT handoffs.
Lazy chaining invariant violation: Mismatched trace variants or register states breaking the canonical address contract, leading to silent data corruption.
Context pointer miscalculation: Incorrect static offset folding for local variables causing stack frame corruption or out-of-bounds memory access.
assessments.summary: High complexity due to low-level register caching, JIT/interpreter state handoffs, and trace chaining invariants. Significant design risk stems from strict boundary synchronization requirements and potential state corruption if dirty register writebacks or offset calculations fail. Requires formal verification to prove trace boundary invariants and lazy chaining safety.
